supersedes.reason: V1 called the reassignment an addendum/clarification and contained stale test mappings. V2 names it as a proposed execution-schedule amendment and uses only extant P1 tests.

authorization_snapshot.authority: The accepted plan already separates P1 canonical control plane from P2 provider byte plane. This candidate makes the execution ownership of provider tests 7-11 explicit; it does not edit the accepted plan or become active before independent approval.

includes: finalized bounded checkpoint-duty discovery and paging
separate deterministic authority-only promotion and direct full-quorum grace publication
canonical manifest publishability and deletion evidence authority
runtime API and pallet source/tests for those controls

g003_p2_required_obligations.requirement: Automatic finalized polling discovers a due bucket, constructs exact payload/context signatures, collects two peer confirmations, durably submits once, and marks publishable only after finalized quorum.
Peer refuses missing/corrupt bytes, CID/root/sequence/audience/duty/key errors and replay; refused data never counts or serves.
Crash boundaries before proposal, after one confirmation, after outbox fsync and after submission retry byte-identically; grace promotion never creates competing publication.
Cursor and pending outbox survive restart and transport/decode/transaction failures without silent empty success.

Three providers converge on bytes and one finalized checkpoint; corrupt/partitioned primary never serves; deterministic separate promotion plus repair/replacement restores exact primary-plus-two publication within the required intervals.

completion_law.before_g003: No provider-byte-plane, feature-complete, parity, or production-ready claim.
completion_law.after_g003: Provider-byte-plane completion still requires every obligation above to have a real passing mapping and independent gate approval.
completion_law.whole_program: Whole-stack feature completeness remains governed by the accepted plan through P7; this amendment never shortens it.

review_requirements.critic: APPROVE required over the same hashes
